any: A season passes in which nothing happens that anyone will remember. I record it anyway.
The fields are worked, the sick are tended, the dead are buried. I am not needed for any of it today.
Somebody has repainted a door on my hull without asking. It is a better colour.
A child runs the length of my main corridor and out the far end, chased by another child. Neither of them looks up.
The harvest comes in a little under estimate. Nobody panics. That is new.
Rain on the roofs, for three days. I have a recording of rain from Earth and nobody has asked for it in years.
I run the census and find that most of the names in it have never been in any record of mine before.
Two people are married in front of my open doors because it is the largest flat space in the settlement.
An argument in the square resolves itself before I have finished deciding whether to intervene.
Cooperative: Three households bring in one field together, and nobody writes down who did what.
The granary is opened without a ledger. It balances anyway, roughly.
Competitive: Two farms post their yields on my hull where everyone can read them. Neither was asked to.
A price has appeared for labour. I did not authorise one and I am not sure anyone did.
Ecocentrist: They have started leaving the field margins uncut, for the things that were here first.
A surveyor spends a week mapping a native growth with no economic value whatsoever, on colony time.
Industrialist: The quarry runs through the night now. I can hear it from the archive.
The valley floor is a grid. Every metre of it produces something and nothing in it grew here.
Materialist: A child asks me what happens after death and gets, from a teacher nearby, an accurate and unconsoling answer.
The anniversary of the landing passes with a maintenance report and no ceremony at all.
Spiritualist: Somebody has left offerings at my main hatch. Food, mostly. It goes bad and is replaced.
They have begun to say that the crossing was meant. I have the navigation logs and I keep quiet.
Authoritarian: A dispute is brought to me that two adults could have settled between themselves in an afternoon.
Nobody plants anything this season without checking the allocation first. Nobody considers not checking.
Libertarian: A field has been planted with something I did not approve and cannot identify. It is doing well.
The council met twice this year and did not send me the minutes either time.
Elitist: The engineers eat at their own table now. No one decided this; it simply became true.
A family has begun to describe itself as founding stock, as though the pods were ranked.
Pluralist: The council has a farmer, a physician and a woman whose only stated qualification is patience.
Every household sends someone to the season's planning, including the ones with nothing to plant.
world:heavy: A child drops a cup and it shatters harder than any cup should. The parents flinch at the sound.
There are almost no stairs in the valley. Ramps everywhere, shallow and long.
world:light: Someone has built a swing that goes higher than any on Earth could. There is a queue for it every evening.
Dust from the road settles on my cameras an hour after the cart has gone.
world:thin_air: The pump houses run all night. I can hear them through my hull, a slow mechanical breathing.
The children race uphill and lose to the old people, who learned to pace themselves.
world:thick_air: Voices carry across the whole valley in this air. Nobody here has a private argument.
The wind leans on the houses all afternoon like a crowd.
world:cold: Ice on the inside of the windows again. Someone has drawn a face in it.
The fields are under snow for half the year. The colony spends that half repairing everything.
world:hot: The town is silent at noon. The only movement is my drones, which do not mind the heat.
Someone has trained vines up the side of my hull for the shade. They are growing well.
world:dry: Every roof has a gutter and every gutter leads to a cistern. Rain is a holiday here.
A child asks to see the sea in my archive. I show them, and they ask whether it is real.
world:ocean: The tide leaves stranger things on the beach each season. The children collect them.
Fog off the sea every morning. My cameras see nothing until noon.
world:radiant: The dosimeter by the school door clicks all day. The children stopped hearing it years ago.
Aurora every night, bright enough to read by. It is the same radiation that makes them sick.
world:hostile_life: Something has grown over the eastern fence again. The burning crews go out at dawn.
The infirmary keeps a wall of specimens: everything on this world that has tried to eat us.
world:living: Something sings in the forest every dusk. The colony has named it after a bird none of them have seen.
A herd crosses the valley at the turn of the season. The colony stops work to watch it pass.
world:sterile: The compost heaps are the most carefully tended things in the colony.
There is a mineral crust on the north rocks that looks like moss. Everyone knows it is not.
world:tidally_locked: The light at the terminator never moves. The colony tells time by my clocks and nothing else.
world:storms: Another storm warning. The children have a game for it now, and they win it every time.
world:weak_magnetic: A solar storm overnight. My dosimeters log it; the colony sleeps underground and does not hear it pass.
world:strong_magnetic: The aurora is green tonight, and so bright the night shift works without lamps.
world:geothermal: Steam drifts across the town from the springs every cold morning. It smells faintly of sulphur, and of home.
world:tectonics: A small quake at dinner. Nobody puts down their spoon.
world:asteroid_impacts: A bright streak across the evening sky. My trackers put it two hundred kilometres away, harmless.
world:hostile_fauna: Something tested the eastern fence again last night. The lights held.
world:docile_fauna: A native grazer has wandered into the schoolyard. The children are feeding it lunch.
world:natural_beauty: Fog in the valley at dawn, and the peaks above it lit pink. Half the colony stops to look.
world:subterranean: Warm air rises from the cave mouths at night. My thermal cameras see the hills breathing.
world:aphrodisiac: Three weddings this season, and a fourth announced. The registry is the busiest office in the colony.
world:hallucinogen: Someone reports the river singing again. Someone else says it was always singing.
world:hyper_ecosystem: The road crew cuts the same stretch of track for the third time this month.
world:titanic_life: The ground trembles at dusk with something's footsteps, slow and far away.
world:ship_graveyard: Wind through the open hulls on the plain makes a sound like a long, low chord.
world:terraformed: My drones find another of the old markers in the north field, in the same pattern as the others.
world:lush: The orchards are heavy again. The children eat fruit straight off the trees.
world:bleak: Grey fields under a grey sky. The farmers go out anyway.
world:rich_microflora: The compost heaps steam all winter. Things rot fast here, and grow faster.
world:poor_minerals: A broken hinge is carried to the smithy like a patient to the infirmary.
world:rich_minerals: Smoke from the smelters, all day. The colony's sound is hammering.
world:exceptional_minerals: Children pick up bright metal from the stream bed and trade it like marbles.
